title: The Science of Deduction
question: Today, can Watson catch Sherlock Holmes out?

stair.described: The staircase and first-floor landing of 221B Baker Street, 1881: seventeen treads in two flights with a half-landing between them, a mahogany banister and turned balusters running up the RIGHT hand, brown patterned stair carpet held down by brass rods, buff striped paper on the walls, a tall sash window on the half-landing giving grey London daylight, a brass gas bracket burning low on the upper wall, and the panelled sitting-room door standing at the head of the flight.
stair.landmark: the panelled sitting-room door at the head of the flight
stair.route: from the foot of the lower flight in the hall, up over the half-landing, to the sitting-room door at the head of the upper flight
stair.geometry: The stair rises from the BOTTOM of frame toward the TOP. The mahogany banister runs up the RIGHT edge of frame with its turned balusters beneath it, and the papered wall runs up the LEFT edge. The tall half-landing window stands in the LEFT wall at the turn, a head and shoulders wide, and the grey daylight from it crosses the carpet. The panelled sitting-room door stands at the TOP of frame at the head of the upper flight and grows from the width of a hand to the full width of frame along the route. The camera keeps to the middle of the treads for every panel, so the banister holds the RIGHT and the wall holds the LEFT.

sofa.described: The sofa corner of the first-floor sitting-room of 221B Baker Street, 1881: two broad sash windows in the FAR wall over Baker Street, a black iron grate under a white marble mantelpiece in the LEFT wall, the panelled door to the landing in the RIGHT wall, a red patterned Turkey carpet, buff striped wallpaper, a horsehair sofa along the near RIGHT wall, two worn armchairs at the hearth, a deal side table carrying a rack of test tubes and a spirit lamp, bookshelves flanking the chimney breast. The horsehair sofa stands along the near RIGHT wall with a drawn heavy red curtain behind its head, its buttoned black seat and rolled arms under a brown rug, and the violin and its bow lie on the seat cushion; the room is dim with the curtain across the nearer window and one low gas jet amber on the wall above.
sofa.landmark: the drawn heavy red curtain at the head of the sofa
sofa.landmark_size: is half the height of the frame
sofa.route: from the foot of the sofa at the room's centre to the drawn curtain at its head against the wall
sofa.geometry: In every panel the camera keeps to the carpet's centre on the near side of the room, so the two broad windows stand in the FAR wall, the marble mantelpiece and its grate stand at the LEFT and the panelled landing door stands at the RIGHT. The sofa runs across the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge with its rolled back against the wall behind it, the buttoned seat filling the lower half of frame. The drawn red curtain hangs behind the sofa's head at the RIGHT of frame from the top edge to the sofa back. The low gas jet burns in a glass shade on the wall at the CENTRE of frame above the sofa back, a thumb tall, standing to the LEFT of the drawn curtain's edge.

hearth.described: The hearth of the first-floor sitting-room of 221B Baker Street, 1881: two broad sash windows in the FAR wall over Baker Street, a black iron grate under a white marble mantelpiece in the LEFT wall, the panelled door to the landing in the RIGHT wall, a red patterned Turkey carpet, buff striped wallpaper, a horsehair sofa along the near RIGHT wall, two worn armchairs at the hearth, a deal side table carrying a rack of test tubes and a spirit lamp, bookshelves flanking the chimney breast. A coal fire burns low in the black iron grate under the white marble mantelpiece in the LEFT wall, a brass fender the width of two spread hands and an iron poker as long as a man's forearm and as thick as one finger stand on the tiled kerb, a worn leather basket chair is drawn up square to the fire with a stack of papers on its arm, and the corner has two light sources, the amber coal fire in the grate at the LEFT and the grey daylight of the two broad windows beyond the chair, each panel naming which of the two lies on the subject.
hearth.landmark: the white marble mantelpiece over the black iron grate
hearth.route: from the basket chair on the carpet to the tiled kerb and the open grate at the chimney breast
hearth.geometry: In every panel the camera keeps to the carpet's centre on the near side of the room, so the two broad windows stand in the FAR wall, the marble mantelpiece and its grate stand at the LEFT and the panelled landing door stands at the RIGHT. The white marble mantelpiece and the black grate beneath it fill the LEFT half of frame from the top edge to the tiled kerb at the bottom. The worn leather basket chair stands in the RIGHT half of frame turned square to that grate. The two broad windows stand small and grey along the TOP RIGHT of frame beyond the chair.

breakfast.described: The breakfast table of the first-floor sitting-room of 221B Baker Street, 1881: two broad sash windows in the FAR wall over Baker Street, a black iron grate under a white marble mantelpiece in the LEFT wall, the panelled door to the landing in the RIGHT wall, a red patterned Turkey carpet, buff striped wallpaper, a horsehair sofa along the near RIGHT wall, two worn armchairs at the hearth, a deal side table carrying a rack of test tubes and a spirit lamp, bookshelves flanking the chimney breast, standing in front of the two broad windows on the morning of the fourth of March: a round table under a white cloth with a toast rack, a coffee pot, two cups, a boiled egg in a cup with a spoon beside it, a butter dish and a folded illustrated magazine; two bentwood chairs drawn up to it, and cold grey window light from behind the table lying along the cloth.
breakfast.landmark: the two broad sash windows behind the table
breakfast.route: from the near edge of the white cloth at the room's centre to the far chair with its back to the windows
breakfast.geometry: In every panel the camera keeps to the carpet's centre on the near side of the room, so the two broad windows stand in the FAR wall, the marble mantelpiece and its grate stand at the LEFT and the panelled landing door stands at the RIGHT. The two broad sash windows fill the upper half of frame behind the table and give the light. The white cloth of the round table runs across the bottom half of frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, with the toast rack and the coffee pot standing on it at the CENTRE. The far bentwood chair stands between the table and the windows.

window.described: The nearer of the two broad sash windows of the first-floor sitting-room of 221B Baker Street, 1881: two broad sash windows in the FAR wall over Baker Street, a black iron grate under a white marble mantelpiece in the LEFT wall, the panelled door to the landing in the RIGHT wall, a red patterned Turkey carpet, buff striped wallpaper, a horsehair sofa along the near RIGHT wall, two worn armchairs at the hearth, a deal side table carrying a rack of test tubes and a spirit lamp, bookshelves flanking the chimney breast, seen from inside the room: twelve panes in two sashes, a brass catch at the meeting rail, heavy red curtains drawn back to either side, a low sill with a plant pot on it, and beyond the glass the roadway of Baker Street below with the opposite pavement, its railings and the plain brick house fronts across the way in grey morning light.
window.landmark: the brass catch at the meeting rail of the two sashes
window.landmark_size: is the height of a finger
window.route: from the carpet a pace back from the window to the sill and the glass itself
window.geometry: In every panel the camera keeps to the carpet's centre on the near side of the room, so the two broad windows stand in the FAR wall, the marble mantelpiece and its grate stand at the LEFT and the panelled landing door stands at the RIGHT. The twelve-paned window fills the whole frame from the top edge to the sill along the bottom, the meeting rail of its two sashes crossing the CENTRE with the brass catch on it. The heavy red curtains hold the LEFT and the RIGHT edges. Through the lower panes the grey roadway and the opposite pavement of Baker Street lie small and far below.
window.crowd: two hansom cabs at a brisk roll on the roadway below, a woman with a basket on the opposite pavement, and a crossing-sweeper at work by the railings

doorway.described: The panelled landing door in the RIGHT wall of the first-floor sitting-room of 221B Baker Street, 1881: two broad sash windows in the FAR wall over Baker Street, a black iron grate under a white marble mantelpiece in the LEFT wall, the panelled door to the landing in the RIGHT wall, a red patterned Turkey carpet, buff striped wallpaper, a horsehair sofa along the near RIGHT wall, two worn armchairs at the hearth, a deal side table carrying a rack of test tubes and a spirit lamp, bookshelves flanking the chimney breast, standing half open onto the dim landing beyond, its brass knob and finger plate catching the light, a mahogany hat stand with a brown bowler on its peg beside the architrave and a folded grey wool shawl two hands long over the peg below it, the red Turkey carpet running up to the threshold, and two light sources on the leaf, the grey window light of the room and the landing's own amber gas bracket burning on the wall beyond the open leaf, each panel naming which of the two lies on the door. A caller in a shabby grey coat and a battered black felt hat stands on the landing boards at the threshold with his back to the camera in the panels that show him, the back of his grey collar and his hat brim the only things of him in frame.
doorway.landmark: the panelled landing door and its brass knob
doorway.route: from the threshold of the landing door to the carpet at the middle of the room
doorway.geometry: In every panel the camera keeps to the carpet's centre on the near side of the room, so the two broad windows stand in the FAR wall, the marble mantelpiece and its grate stand at the LEFT and the panelled landing door stands at the RIGHT. In every panel turned at the threshold -- the panels showing the caller's grey-coated back and the panels showing the commissionaire's face -- the panelled landing door and its architrave hold the RIGHT half of frame from the top edge to the carpet at the bottom, the brass knob at hand height on its inner edge, the mahogany hat stand against the wall in the RIGHT corner beside it, the red carpet running from the threshold across the bottom of frame to the LEFT edge, and the two broad windows small at the TOP LEFT. In the reverse panels, the ones showing Watson's face, the room itself stands behind him: the white marble mantelpiece and its dark grate hold the LEFT edge behind his shoulder, the two broad sash windows stand small and grey at the TOP LEFT, the buff striped paper of the near wall fills the CENTRE and the RIGHT behind his ear, and the red Turkey carpet holds the bottom edge. Watson's eyes are turned to the RIGHT of frame and the commissionaire's eyes a thumb's width to the LEFT of the lens, so the two eyelines cross and each man looks at the other across the cut. The dim landing beyond the open leaf grows narrower along the route: a hand wide at the threshold, two fingers wide a pace inside the room, a thumb's width in the closest panel on the commissionaire's face, and a finger's width in the salute.

shots.why: Opens the episode on the move-in: the bargain is already struck, and Watson is committed before he knows anything.

shots.why: Establishes the narrator's own emptiness, the appetite the whole chapter feeds; a scene shows the protagonist as well as the news.

cuts.frame: Insert square photograph at the half-landing: the polished silver ball knob of a black walking stick, the knob the size of a plum, standing over the brown patterned carpet with the shaft plumb beside a brown boot, the shaft as thick as one finger, cold grey light from the tall sash window lying along the silver and the boot's toecap.

shots.turn: a guess invited -> a verdict delivered
shots.why: Holmes answers a question nobody has finished asking, and does it without leaving the fire.

shots.at_rest: Watson stands on the red Turkey carpet a hand's breadth from the sill, his head turned a quarter round from the glass toward the room, his chin level, his eyes narrowed on the roadway still. shots.why: Sets the wager the button settles, and shows Watson's own vanity, the quality the ending punishes.

shots.at_rest: Watson stands at the CENTRE of frame, his head and both shoulders filling it, his eyes turned to the RIGHT. His dark hair is swept back above a sunburnt face and a thin waxed moustache. His bare sunburnt right hand rests closed on the watch chain across his tweed waistcoat below the bottom edge, brown to the wrist. shots.turn: a test set -> the test put
shots.why: Watson springs his trap, in the blandest voice he has; the episode's question is asked out loud here.

shots.frame: Medium close on Watson with the white marble mantelpiece and the bookshelf of the chimney breast at the LEFT edge behind him, bare-headed, his dark hair swept back, a thin waxed moustache on a sunburnt face, his mouth closed and level under it, the white cravat at his throat, his RIGHT shoulder alone in frame at the bottom, his lips together with the line on them.

shots.turn: a win -> one more question
shots.why: Watson pushes his luck one question too far, which is how the world gets to answer him.

shots.frame: Close on the commissionaire's broad weather-beaten red-brown face and squared shoulders, bare-headed with close-cropped grizzled grey hair, a heavy clean-shaven jaw and a thick neck, his small dark eyes straight into the camera, the plain dark brown sack coat buttoned high to the stand collar with the black neckerchief knotted at his throat, the open door leaf behind him at the RIGHT with a finger's width of the dim landing beyond its edge, his lips together with the line on them.

The face fills the CENTRE, the small dark eyes straight into the camera under the heavy brows, the clean-shaven upper lip and the heavy jaw below it. The squared shoulder line runs to both edges across the bottom third, the stand collar close at the throat, a finger's width of the dim landing at the RIGHT edge.

shots.turn: Watson right -> Holmes right
shots.why: THE BUTTON: the world answers, in the mouth of a man who has no idea what he has settled.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: We took the rooms next day and were installed there by the second morning.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: My life had no object in it, and nobody called on me but him.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: For days on end he lay on that sofa and hardly uttered a word from morning to night.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: There was a dreamy, vacant look in his eyes that I could not account for.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Then the working fit would take him, and the fiddle scraped half the night.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: So one evening I took a pencil and wrote down everything the man knew.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Chemistry, profound. Anatomy, accurate. Astronomy, nil — he had never heard of Copernicus.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: I could find no trade on earth that wanted all of it, so I burned the list.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: On the fourth of March I came down early; he was still at breakfast.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: An article said a man's whole history shows in his cuffs and boots.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Ineffable twaddle, I said, and slapped the magazine down beside the toast rack.

lines.speaker: sherlock_holmes
lines.text: You would lose your money. I wrote that article myself.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: I had called his own work rubbish over his own toast.

lines.speaker: sherlock_holmes
lines.text: I am a consulting detective. The only one in the world.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Strangers came at all hours. He called them clients and asked me to step out.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Clever, I thought, and conceited past bearing. So I changed the subject and tried him.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: A big plain-dressed fellow on the far pavement, a blue envelope in his hand.

lines.speaker: sherlock_holmes
lines.text: You mean the retired sergeant of Marines.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Brag and bounce, I thought. He knew perfectly well I could not check a word.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: A loud knock below. A deep voice in the hall. Heavy boots on our seventeen stairs.

lines.speaker: unnamed_retired_marine_sergeant
lines.text: For Mr. Sherlock Holmes.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: And what is your trade, my lad?

lines.speaker: unnamed_retired_marine_sergeant
lines.text: Commissionaire, sir. Uniform away for repairs.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: And before that, my lad?

lines.speaker: unnamed_retired_marine_sergeant
lines.text: A sergeant, sir. Royal Marine Light Infantry, sir.
